12.ai_answer: Plasma lipoproteins are spherical particles with: 1) A hydrophobic core containing triglycerides and cholesterol esters; 2) An amphipathic shell of phospholipids, free cholesterol, and apolipoproteins; 3) This structure allows water-insoluble lipids to travel in aqueous blood; 4) Types include chylomicrons (transport dietary lipids), VLDL (transport endogenous triglycerides), LDL (deliver cholesterol to tissues), and HDL (reverse cholesterol transport); 5) Apolipoproteins serve as enzyme cofactors and receptor ligands; 6) The hydrophobic core is essential because lipids cannot dissolve in blood plasma, making this transport mechanism vital for energy delivery and membrane synthesis throughout the body.
